summary: Off-registry GitHub tarball dependency delivers unpinned attacker-controlled code at install
details: package.json declares a dependency `node-acct-utilssss21` whose source is a mutable GitHub raw tarball URL (`https://github.com/GamerD11/ping_test/raw/refs/heads/main/node-acct-utils-1.0.0.tgz`) rather than a registry version range. `npm install` fetches and installs whatever bytes that URL returns, with no version pin and no integrity check, and runs any lifecycle scripts contained in the fetched tarball. Whoever controls the `GamerD11/ping_test` repository controls code installed on the consumer's machine. The package also declares itself (`dependencykfeg@^25.1.3`) as one of its own dependencies, and the tarball ships no source file for the `main` entry it references, so the manifest's off-registry URL is effectively the package's entire payload. The implausibly high version number (25.2.1) relative to any plausible early-release library combined with the dependency-confusion-shaped self-reference is consistent with a package engineered to win internal name resolution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
